extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political philosophy, theology, and readers of Hobbes' Leviathan
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from a political-theological treatise (Hobbes' Leviathan) arguing for the supremacy of the civil sovereign over ecclesiastical authorities and setting out what is necessary for salvation (faith and obedience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of Bishops derived from Civil Sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jurisdiction of Bishops, is derived from the Civill Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: inequality of bishops' jurisdictions (some preside over a town, others over many provinces) shows jurisdiction was not determined by God's command but assigned by human princes; historical practice (emperors of Rome granting jurisdiction) supports this. Exception only where the Pope is also the civil sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal jurisdiction is not De Jure Divino universally
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither hath the Pope his De Jure Divino, except onely where hee is also the Civill Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim that the Pope holds universal divine right is denied unless he is also civil sovereign in that territory; the Pope may exercise powers within his own dominions or where princes have granted him authority, but not universally by divine ordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil sovereign is the natural source of jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Law of Nature ... the Civill Soveraign in every Common-wealth, is the Head, the Source, the Root, and the Sun, from which all Jurisdiction is derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereignty originates in the consent of those governed (or by conquest) and is the 'soul' that holds the commonwealth together; thus both temporal and spiritual officers ultimately depend on the civil sovereign for jurisdiction in that polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality of ecclesiastical jurisdictions implies human origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences — some are Bishops but of own Town, some of a hundred Towns, and some of many whole Provinces; which differences were not determined by the command of God; their Jurisdiction therefore is not of God, but of Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of empirical/historical observation (variation in jurisdictional scope) as proof that ecclesiastical authority is instituted by human political arrangements, not by uniform divine grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pope has no direct supreme temporal power over other princes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pope (without his owne Territory) has not any Temporall Jurisdiction DIRECTLY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While historical canons and papal acts sometimes asserted or effected temporal interventions (e.g., Lateran canon, depositions, transfers), such practices do not establish a natural or divine right for the Pope to depose or govern other princes directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of a legitimate 'indirect' papal temporal right to depose princes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pope has (in the Dominions of other Princes) the Supreme Temporall Power INDIRECTLY: which is denyed; unlesse he mean by Indirectly, that he has gotten it by Indirect means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'indirectly' is meant as 'acquired by human means' that is true; but the claim that temporal jurisdiction is a necessary consequence of pastoral (spiritual) power and thus gives the Pope the right to change kingdoms is rejected as unjust and dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between temporal and spiritual power is nominal
rubrics_metrics.description: This distinction of Temporall, and Spirituall Power is but words. Power is as really divided, and as dangerously to all purposes, by sharing with another Indirect Power, as with a Direct one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing or dividing authority—whether direct or 'indirect'—threatens effective sovereignty; civil rulers should consider the practical and moral consequences of admitting divided authority (e.g., competing obligations of subjects).

rubrics_metrics.name: You cannot infer subjection of persons from subordination of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Subordination of an Art, cannot be inferred the Subjection of the Professor; so from the Subordination of a Government, cannot be inferred the Subjection of the Governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if spiritual ends are higher (means-to-end relation), that does not make civil governors subject to spiritual governors; subordination of offices or functions does not yield personal subjection or political obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: There is no spiritual commonwealth on earth; kingdom of Christ is not of this world
rubrics_metrics.description: Spirituall Common-wealth there is none in this world: for it is the same thing with the Kingdome of Christ; which he himselfe saith, is not of this world; but shall be in the next world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the kingdom of Christ is eschatological, there is no autonomous, earthly 'spiritual commonwealth' that can legitimately exercise temporal sovereign power over earthly states.

rubrics_metrics.name: When commands conflict, obey God rather than man if known to be God's
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man receiveth two contrary Commands, and knows that one of them is Gods, he ought to obey that, and not the other, though it be the command even of his lawfull Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practical problem is discerning whether a command is genuinely from God or a human abusing God's name; only when a command truly requires betrayal of eternal salvation may one disobey civil authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: All that is necessary to salvation: faith in Christ and obedience to laws
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is NECESSARY to Salvation, is contained in two Vertues, Faith in Christ, and Obedience to Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obedience (if perfect) would suffice, but because humans have sinned, remission of sins by faith in Christ is required; nothing beyond faith and obedience is strictly necessary for salvation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience is the will/endeavour to obey (accepting the will for the deed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Obedience required ... is a serious Endeavour to Obey him; and is called also by all such names as signifie that Endeavour ... called Charity, and Love, ... Righteousnesse; ... Repentance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obedience includes internal disposition (love, repentance) and the will to conform to God's commandments; in practice, willing obedience and repentance are what the law requires given human imperfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws of God are the laws of Nature and the laws of civil sovereigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The Laws of God therefore are none but the Laws of Nature, whereof the principall is, that we should not violate our Faith, that is, a commandement to obey our Civill Soveraigns ... and the Laws of our severall Soveraigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ gave counsel and exposition rather than new civil laws; biblical precepts are binding as law only insofar as the civil sovereign has made them public law; otherwise they are counsel which a man may refuse at his peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: The person to be believed in absence of special revelation is the Supreme Pastor (civil sovereign)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Person which all they that have no speciall revelation are to beleeve, is (in every Common-wealth) the Supreme Pastor, that is to say, the Civill Soveraigne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faith 'comes by hearing' the lawful pastors; since private supernatural revelation is exceptional, ordinary people must accept the teaching of those appointed (ultimately the sovereign's ordained pastors) as the source of religious instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith comes by hearing; teachers are the ordinary means though faith is a gift of God
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the Doctrine of St. Paul ... 'Faith cometh by Hearing' ... the ordinary immediate cause of our beleef ... is Hearing our lawfull Pastors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: public preaching and authorized teachers are the ordinary instruments by which people come to believe scripture and doctrines; nonetheless faith itself remains a divine gift and not purely the effect of human teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only necessary article of Christian faith for salvation: Jesus is the Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Onely Article of Faith, which the Scripture maketh simply Necessary to Salvation, is this, that JESUS IS THE CHRIST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes will argue from the scope of the evangelists that the recognition of Jesus as the promised Christ is the single article strictly necessary for salvation; other articles may be important but are not strictly necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects are not competent judges of heresy; determination belongs to the sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: To judge whether a King draw his subjects to Haeresie, belongeth to the Pope. ... Nor is there any Judge of Haeresie amongst Subjects, but their own Civill Soveraign; for 'Haeresie is nothing else, but a private opinion, obstinately maintained, contrary to the opinion which the Publique Person ... hath commanded to bee taught.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heresy is defined relative to the public teaching authorized by the sovereign; private persons lack legitimate authority to judge or depose rulers on heresy grounds, and toleration of heterodox rulers is a question subordinate to duties of faith and civil faithfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical examples and papal acts do not alone prove legitimate authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples prove nothing; ... the Examples he alledgeth make not so much as a probability of Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution against reasoning from precedent or the fact that popes historically exercised power: acts performed in their own cause (e.g., excommunications, depositions) are invalid proofs of a divine right and may be crimes rather than legitimating events.

rubrics_metrics.name: It is unjust to depose a lawfully chosen king even if non-Christian
rubrics_metrics.description: To choose him, may in some cases bee unjust; but to depose him, when he is chosen, is in no case Just. For it is alwaies violation of faith, and consequently against the Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a king is non-Christian or holds erroneous doctrines, subjects obeying him does not automatically justify deposition; deposing a chosen sovereign violates the covenant/faith that established his authority and is therefore unjust.
